title: Simultaneous Duration: miközben, mialatt, and eközben

sections.title: Parallel Action with Subordinate 'miközben' and 'mialatt'
sections.content: Hungarian uses 'miközben' (while / in the course of) and 'mialatt' (during the time that / while) to link two events occurring simultaneously. 'Miközben' emphasizes concurrent activity, often setting a background action against a foreground event: 'A madár körözött, miközben a solymász lentről figyelte.' 'Mialatt' highlights the span of elapsed time throughout which the action continues.

sections.title: Independent Discourse Sequencing with 'eközben'
sections.content: 'Eközben' is an adverb meaning 'meanwhile / in the meantime'. Unlike 'miközben', it does not introduce a subordinate clause; instead, it starts a new independent clause or sentence: 'A solymász a madarat etette. Eközben a narrátor a füzetébe jegyzetelt.' In film analysis, 'eközben' establishes cross-cutting between two parallel scenes.

sections.title: Simultaneity Markers at B2
rows: while / in the course of (concurrent parallel action)
during the time that / while (emphasis on elapsed duration)
meanwhile / in the meantime (independent discourse adverb)

items.spanish: Miközben a kamera lassan mozgott, a zene fokozta a feszültséget.
items.english: While the camera moved slowly, the music heightened the tension.

items.spanish: Mialatt a segéd a húst vágta, a narrátor a dúcokat vizsgálta.
items.english: While the assistant was cutting the meat, the narrator examined the roosts.

items.spanish: Lilik a mezőn gyakorolt; eközben a telepen csend honolt.
items.english: Lilik was practicing in the field; meanwhile, silence reigned at the station.

items.spanish: A festmény sötét háttere még élesebben kiemeli a főalakot.
items.english: The painting's dark background highlights the main figure even more sharply.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Distinguish grammar clearly: 'miközben' requires a comma before it as a conjunction, while 'eközben' begins an independent sentence or follows a semicolon.
